implemented_capabilities.capability: Evidence provenance, freshness and scope-completeness judgement (fail-closed)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Every evidence edge carries id/verified/observed_at/valid_until/evidence_source; judge() returns fresh|stale|unverified against one evaluation time. collect_evidence() runs named read-only Cypher per tier, records every query (template, rows, latency) and turns stale, unverified, uncollected, duplicate-id, contradictory or failed-query evidence into INCONCLUSIVE reasons so absence is never confused with missing data.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Time-bound, snapshot-hashed verification certificate with supersession and expiry
implemented_capabilities.notes: A certificate expires at min(earliest evidence valid_until, issue+24h) and becomes SUPERSEDED the moment Meta.revision of the sandbox differs from certificate.sandbox_revision. It binds to SHA-256 of a canonical, paged, id-checked graph export (nodes+edges, derived ATTACK_STEP excluded) and records engine sha, FalkorDB version and audit hash.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Revision compare-and-set mutation with graph-level locking (dependency invalidation by revision bump)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Each mutation is one Cypher query 'MATCH (m:Meta) WHERE m.revision=$expected ... SET m.revision=m.revision+1' under a Redis-keyspace lock; any change invalidates all certificates and derived ATTACK_STEP edges. sandbox_ops supports EXPOSE_WORKLOAD, ADD_LATERAL_REACH and EXPIRE_EVIDENCE (forces a valid_until into the past) with typed validation.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Tamper-evident hash-chained audit log in Redis Streams
implemented_capabilities.notes: hash_N = SHA256(payload_hash_N || hash_{N-1}); appends are serialised by a cross-process lock; verify() replays the chain and detects insert/delete/modify. Stored in XADD stream with 7-day PEXPIRE retention.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Approval-gating Action Gateway (allowlist, idempotency, revision and certificate checks)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Ordered checks: action allowlist, SIMULATION-only mode, idempotency key regex + cached receipt, certificate belongs to this plan, sandbox_revision == current revision, certificate VALID. Every rejection and receipt is appended to the audit chain. Execution is a simulation receipt only; no infrastructure is touched.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Internet-to-crown-jewel ATTACK_STEP derivation, bounded chain enumeration, FalkorDB max-flow and independent oracle BFS
implemented_capabilities.notes: Cypher CREATEs ENTRY/LATERAL/GOAL ATTACK_STEP edges (MITRE T1190/T1210/T1078.004 labels) only when evidence scope is complete; enumerates chains with CAN_REACH*0..3; uses FalkorDB algo.maxFlow and algo.bfs; a pure-Python BFS oracle cross-checks; hunter copies the graph (GRAPH.COPY), prunes flows under candidate policies, requires E/F/O agreement for up to 5 rounds before issuing a certificate.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Exact bounded minimum-impact remediation search (hitting-set over bitmasks)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Enumerates all plans of at most 3 egress-allowlist actions from a catalogue capped at 30 using bitmask coverage of the chain constraint set; lexicographic objective (declared deps broken, unknown impact, action count, flows blocked, ids). Optimality is explicitly 'EXACT_WITHIN_K', not global.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Alert-storm triage into ON_ATTACK_PATH / NOT_ON_ATTACK_PATH / NOT_ACTIONABLE / TRIAGE_INCONCLUSIVE with clustering
implemented_capabilities.notes: Cross-checks FalkorDB BFS against the Python reachability and fails closed with METHOD_DISAGREEMENT; alerts with stale or unverified vulnerability evidence become TRIAGE_INCONCLUSIVE rather than being dismissed.

implemented_capabilities.capability: FalkorDB graph store utilities: named-graph copy under global lock with fork-retry, RENAMENX, TTL, version probe
implemented_capabilities.notes: Handles the FalkorDB 'could not fork' quirk with a Redis owner-token lock and exponential backoff; run() maps timeouts and truncated results (row_limit reached) to QueryFailedError so truncation is never trusted. Verified against falkordb server 4.22.1.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Investigation memory graph (Plan, Certificate, Asset nodes, recalled but re-verified)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Per-session memory graph stores (Plan)-[:PROTECTS]->(Asset) and (Plan)-[:CERTIFIED_BY]->(Certificate) with sandbox_revision, so recall can compare the remembered revision to the current one; failures degrade to UNAVAILABLE and never break a run.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Claude tool-use investigation agent over a 7-tool MCP server with code-enforced guards
implemented_capabilities.notes: LLM only narrates and picks tools; status/plan/certificate/receipt are copied from tool results, containment wording without SIMULATED_CONTAINMENT is flagged, 12 tool-call/14 turn/180 s caps, deterministic fallback pipeline when the API fails. Requires an Anthropic API key; the environment is fully synthetic.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Synthetic cloud/K8s environment generator and loader
implemented_capabilities.notes: All pods, CVEs, IAM roles and alerts are generated demo data (evidence_source 'SYNTHETIC_GENERATOR'); the 'collector' that stamps observed_at/valid_until in stamp_evidence is a synthetic re-stamp, not a real scanner.

graph_models_and_cypher: Labels: Meta{id:'meta',revision,inventory_complete,storm_id}, Pod, Service, Ingress, Internet, ContainerImage, Vulnerability{status,attack_vector,cvss_score}, Database{is_crown_jewel}, IAMRole, IAMPermission{effect}, NetworkPolicy{status:'CANDIDATE', managed_by}, Alert; memory graph: Plan, Certificate, Asset. Edges: EXPOSES, ROUTES_TO, TARGETS, RUNS_IMAGE, HAS_VULNERABILITY, CAN_REACH, ASSUMES_ROLE, GRANTS_ACCESS, APPLIES_TO, SELECTS, ALLOWS_EGRESS, DEPENDS_ON, ON_WORKLOAD, REFERENCES, derived ATTACK_STEP{kind,capacity,backing_evidence_ids,built_at_revision,technique_id}, PROTECTS, CERTIFIED_BY. Every evidence edge has id, verified, observed_at, valid_until, evidence_source. Uses FalkorDB-native procedures algo.bfs and algo.maxFlow (not Neo4j GDS/APOC), GRAPH.COPY, ro_query with per-query timeout, FOREACH delete, UNWIND bulk create, variable-length CAN_REACH*0..N (N int()-cast), labels(), properties(), collect(DISTINCT). Cypher is parameterised; only constant fragments or whitelisted identifiers are interpolated.
algorithms: Layered attack-step graph built from evidence with backing_evidence_ids per edge (engine/attackgraph.py:build_attack_steps) and revision stamping
Bounded chain enumeration with variable-length CAN_REACH*0..3 and node-sequence de-dup, CHAIN_ENUM_CAP 10,000 (attackgraph.py:enumerate_chains)
Unit-capacity max-flow via algo.maxFlow = edge-disjoint path count, flow decomposition into paths with cycle removal (attackgraph.py:max_flow, hunter.py:decompose)
Three-method agreement rule E (bounded chains) / F (max-flow) / O (pure-Python BFS) before certification (hunter.py:disagreement, interdict_oracle/reachability.py)
Iterative CEGAR-like re-planning loop, max 5 rounds, residual paths added to the constraint set (hunter.py:hunt)
Exact bounded hitting-set search with bitmask coverage and lexicographic cost (planner.py:solve)
Hash-chained append-only log (audit.py) and canonical graph hashing (snapshot.py)
Compare-and-set revision counter for optimistic concurrency (sandbox.py:mutate)

agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Claude tool-use loop (agent.py:run_agent) over MCP tools with hard budgets and a deterministic fallback pipeline (investigation.py). Memory is a per-session FalkorDB graph of dated Plan/Certificate/Asset nodes recalled first and always re-verified (memory.py). Evidence-tier state machine: CollectionStatus (COLLECTED_COMPLETE/EMPTY, QUERY_FAILED, STALE_EXPIRED, UNCOLLECTED) -> InvestigationStatus/PlanStatus/SimulationStatus -> CertificateStatus (VALID, EXPIRED, SUPERSEDED, REVERIFICATION_FAILED). Session isolation via HMAC-derived graph keys never accepted from clients.
tests_present: backend/tests: 14 pytest files, roughly 167 test functions (test_hunter 23, test_planner 25, test_services 16, test_falkordb_contract 15, test_evidence 14, test_seed_generator 12, test_triage 11, test_attack_paths 10, test_api 9, test_mcp_agent 9, test_oracle_reachability 7, test_graphstore 6, test_seed_loader 6, test_snapshot 4); they need a live FalkorDB 4.22.1 (CI service container pinned by digest). test_falkordb_contract.py pins FalkorDB quirks (silent result truncation, maxFlow erroring on absent rel type, outgoing-only BFS, copy refusing existing dst). Frontend has vitest/RTL tests (http, sha256, stream, Num, UntrustedText, derive, status, pages, WorkbenchPage).
dependency_requirements: anthropic==1.13.0 (optional at runtime; agent disabled when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset)
security_findings: backend/src/interdict/api.py:681 - reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from environment (no hard-coded key found); sends alert/graph-derived context to Anthropic API when enabled

backend/src/interdict/engine/attackgraph.py:334 - f-string Cypher interpolating max_lateral_hops, but cast with int() and range-checked 0..3 (not injectable); lines 36-69 use .format() on constant fragments only
backend/src/interdict/seed/loader.py:107-204 - f-string Cypher with labels/relationship types passed through _identifier() validator (not user-controlled)

backend/src/interdict/engine/sandbox.py:142-146 and sandbox_ops.py:106,178 - mutate() concatenates a 'body' Cypher fragment; all callers pass constant fragments with $params (not injectable today, but a footgun if body ever comes from input)
backend/src/interdict/graphstore.py:110 - Redis EVAL of a fixed Lua release-if-owner script (safe)
backend/src/interdict/api.py:127-194 - HMAC cookie + CSRF token signing with server secret; config.py:70-79 refuses to start with secrets <32 chars (good practice, no hard-coded secret)
backend/src/interdict/mcp_server.py:70-78 - MCP tools require Bearer internal token (hmac.compare_digest) and session header; sandbox mutation operations are deliberately not exposed as MCP tools
backend/src/interdict/audit.py - tamper-evident only; anyone controlling Redis can rewrite the whole chain (documented in module docstring)
No subprocess, eval/exec, pickle or shell execution found in backend/src; no unrestricted outbound HTTP except the Anthropic client
duplicates_or_overlaps: Attack-path / blast-radius traversal (Security & Vulnerability family); remediation planning; alert triage; certificate/approval gating overlaps with any decision-lineage or evidence-drift engine; graph-memory family. Overlaps with Argus/blastradius-style traversal repos but is far deeper on evidence freshness and verification.
evidence_drift_relevance: HIGH - implements per-edge provenance with observed_at/valid_until/verified/evidence_source, a fail-closed freshness judge, certificates that become SUPERSEDED on any graph revision change or EXPIRED when the earliest underlying evidence ages out, snapshot hashing, an approval-gating gateway and a hash-chained audit log, which are the core primitives of an Evidence Drift Cascade engine.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Domain-neutral parts (freshness/verification judge, completeness-before-verdict rule, revision CAS, certificate supersession/expiry, canonical graph hashing, hash-chained audit, gating gateway, FalkorDB lock/copy handling) are written for the exact stack Kairos runs (FalkorDB 4.22 + falkordb client + FastAPI + Python 3.12) and are covered by live-graph tests. Only the K8s/attack-path queries are domain-specific.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB 4.22.x (Redis-backed; uses redis client directly for locks/streams); Anthropic key only for the optional agent

strategy_rationale: The evidence-judgement, revision-CAS, certificate-lifecycle, snapshot-hash, audit-chain and gateway modules are domain-neutral and map directly onto an Evidence Drift Cascade engine, so they should be lifted into a shared Kairos engine with the Pod/Vulnerability queries replaced by Kairos labels. The attack-path/planner/hunter stack can be offered as a Security domain pack on top.
